text: [ON HOLD until 19 Dec 2026, superseded by n20261121protocol] STOP AND TRAIL RULE (from MSS Nov 20). MSS: bought 100 at 1.19 (16:51Z), trailing stop $0.10 filled 1.17 at 17:01Z on a dip to 1.12 (-$4.00 net). It then broke 1.30 at 17:15Z, ran to 1.62 (17:22Z) with two volatility halts. Replay on 1-min bars: $0.10 trail stopped at 1.17; $0.15 trail would have hit at exactly 1.12 (about -$9); $0.16-0.20 would have survived and exited near 1.42-1.46 (about +$20-25 on 100 sh). MSS normal pullbacks were $0.10-0.15 (1.25->1.12, 1.31->1.22). RULE: 1) Initial stop = structural, under the last swing low or VWAP, not a fixed cent amount. 2) Switch to a trailing stop only once the trade is up at least one normal pullback. 3) Trail width = about 1.5x the stock's typical 1-min high-to-low pullback over the last 30 min (roughly 12-15% on sub-$2 names); never inside the normal pullback range. 4) Shares = (2% of net liquidation - $2 commission) / stop distance, capped by settled cash; a wider stop means fewer shares (MSS at $0.18 trail = about 35 shares, not 100). 5) Sell half at the first target with a limit order; when it fills, reduce the trailing stop to the remaining shares. 6) Never place an order into a halt reopen; wait 5 minutes of trading.
